title: Strategic rhythm and OKR linkage for Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Summary: Define a repeatable quarterly rhythm that ties the Hosted API roadmap and Model Catalog lifecycle to company OKRs and product priorities. Outcome: a single source-of-truth cadence (planning -> commitment -> execution -> review) with mapped owners, deliverables, and measurable signals for each initiative.

Scope: hosted API product features (SDK changes, structured output, rate-limits), model catalog policies (model additions/removals, gating, performance profiles), rollout playbooks (canary/A-B, rollback), and OKR alignment artifacts. Excludes detailed engineering tickets which will be created as dependencies.

Goals: 1) Create a one-page quarterly planning template that maps initiatives to OKRs, success metrics, release windows, and risk mitigation plans. 2) Standardize a two-week planning cadence with cross-functional checkpoints (PM/Eng/Design/Research/Compliance). 3) Produce a retrospective checklist and sprint review template to capture model regressions and cost/latency regressions for next quarter.

Acceptance criteria: - Template live in Confluence and referenced in Console/roadmap dashboards. - At least 3 model-catalog model lifecycle rules (onboarding, deprecation, emergency rollback) documented and approved by Research/Infra. - OKR mapping spreadsheet populated for Q2 2026 with owners and target metrics. - Stakeholder sign-off (Eng leadership, Product, Design, Research, Sales) recorded in comments.

Deliverables: - Confluence planning template (milestones, owners, metrics). - Quarter plan artifact (CSV/Sheet) for import into roadmap tooling. - One-pager for exec review summarizing trade-offs and recommended prioritization. - Playbook snippets for canary rollouts and model fallback policies.

Trade-offs and risks: - Tighter model gating reduces churn but increases review latency; propose staged gating for high-risk model changes. - Stronger batching/quantization suggestions improve cost but may introduce subtle quality regressions—require eval gates. - Dependencies on infra autoscaling work may shift timelines for throughput-sensitive features.

Stakeholders: Diego Morales (owner), Anika Shah (PM sponsor), Priya Ramesh (Research), Marcus Nguyen (Infra), Lina Duarte (Design), Sales/CS reps for customer impact context.

Acceptance metrics: initiative coverage in roadmap (>=90%), OKR target definitions for top 4 initiatives, and an initial run of retrospective capturing at least 3 concrete action items tied to operational dashboards.

Notes and links: See attachments for draft template, kickoff deck, and example OKR mapping.
